concepts.title: Subject-Verb Agreement: Advanced
concepts.definition: Advanced agreement rules: two nouns naming one dish or idea take a singular verb; with either-or and neither-nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject; distances, sums and quantities treated as one unit stay singular.
concepts.formula: either A or B -> verb agrees with B (the nearer subject)
concepts.key_idea: Find the nearest subject after or and nor; treat one-unit quantities as singular.
question_patterns: Fill in the blank with the verb that agrees with the subject
Choose is or are, was or were for the sentence
Complete the sentence so the verb agrees

solution_steps.explain: bread and butter, ten kilometres -> singular
either-or / neither-nor agree with the second subject
one of my friends -> he lives -> lives

worked_examples.q: Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: Bread and butter ___ my usual breakfast. (be)
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: Either Ritu or her brothers ___ responsible for the delay. (be)
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: Ten kilometres ___ a long walk for a child. (be)
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: One of my friends ___ in Delhi. (live)
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: The quality of the mangoes ___ good this time. (be)
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: Neither the players nor the coach ___ satisfied with the result. (be)
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form: Each of the students ___ a certificate today. (receive)

concepts.title: Synonyms and Antonyms: Choose the Word
concepts.definition: A synonym means the same, an antonym means the opposite. The options are printed in the question - pick the one word that fits the asked relation.
concepts.formula: synonym = same meaning;  antonym = opposite meaning
concepts.key_idea: Replace the word in a short phrase to test the meaning before choosing.
question_patterns: Choose the synonym of the given word from the options
Choose the antonym of the given word from the options
Pick the word that matches or opposes the given word

solution_steps.explain: same meaning for a synonym, opposite for an antonym
a related word is not a synonym

worked_examples.q: Choose the synonym of 'brave': (timid, courageous, careless)
Choose the synonym of 'huge': (tiny, enormous, narrow)
Choose the antonym of 'ancient': (modern, antique, aged)
Choose the antonym of 'abundant': (plentiful, scarce, ample)
Choose the synonym of 'fortunate': (lucky, unlucky, poor)
Choose the antonym of 'victory': (triumph, defeat, success)
Choose the synonym of 'begin': (finish, commence, pause)

concepts.title: Correct Spelling: Advanced
concepts.definition: Four spellings of one harder word are given; only one is correct. Watch double consonants, silent letters and -ence versus -ance endings.
concepts.formula: occ-as-ion? no: occasion has two c, two s? one c? learn: occasion, maintenance, privilege
concepts.key_idea: Break the word into syllables and count every consonant.
question_patterns: Choose the correctly spelled word from the four options
Pick the right spelling of the word
Which option spells the word correctly?
